Google threatened to remove websites from its search engine unless they let Google use their content - Business Insider

The Wall Street Journal on Thursday published excerpts from a 2012 Federal Trade Commission document. The document was part of the FTC's investigation of Google after complaints from competitors. It was never meant to be public but was accidentally sent to The Journal after a Freedom of Information Act request.

From the FTC report:

When competitors asked Google to stop taking their content, it threatened to remove them from its search engine.

BI further notes:

Google eventually offered to let websites opt out of including their content in Google's search results, among other changes.

Perhaps we should enact a regular election for moderators and recall for those moderators.

The elections could be directly democratic and be limited to one vote per IP. Voat voting could have requirements too, perhaps your account must be:

  1. Account is more than ~6 months old.

  2. Account has been used in the past week.

  3. Account is not banned from any subverse for a major reason.

  4. Account has submitted ~5 posts or comments.

Perhaps there could be an increasing vote value to older accounts as long as they stay in regular use. This could incentivise people to keep one account and encourage users who have been here longer to vote for what they believe contributes to the common good. On this site we should attempt to let the users have power and decide the site-wide rules as well as the ones on smaller subverses.

We all need to remember that this is OUR site and that we should attempt to set up a system like this to support our interests and to differentiate ourselves from reddit and make an internet forum democracy for ourselves.

I also believe Voat could also benefit from a judicial system where (elected) site admins can take major dissenters to an online courtroom where they can publically argue in view of the whole site if they actually broke site rules or not. Finding an unbiased jury with be difficult on a site where information is meant to be spread fast and efficiently. Perhaps we could do away with a limited jury and use the site populus as a jury where a supermajority must be reached for a conclusion to be achieved.

A major problem with this system is that people cannot see a candidate's personality without actually knowing the user. However, major contributors to subverses will probably and rightfully get their place on that subverse's moderator staff. And even if a mod does not deserve to be on the mod bench, any user who meets the voting requirements can send a request to the judicial section for a referendum to recall the unfit moderator or administrator.

I don't believe there should be term limits for the elections because mods who do their job successfully will continue to do so, and if they don't, they'll be recalled or simply not voted back into moderation. I believe that appointed moderators and admins have much a higher possibility to ruin a forum than actual users who attempt to help their community by running for elections and becoming moderators for subverses they are actually interested in.

No, You Can't Upgrade from Pirated Windows to 'Legit' Windows 10

What's the point of that then?

If you downloaded it before, then chances are you will download it again so that you don't get the 'lite' version of windows.

I think it's two things: to reward already existing users with a free upgrade, and to still maintain their business model. Pirates are going to pirate anyway, so there's no reason to reward them. Very few people buy Windows, so they just stick on the old version they've got (I just encountered XP on my bosses' old laptop). Giving away Win10 to existing users means more people will remain invested in that ecosystem, which gives MS money, especially for Office and the Windows Store.

That said, they still want to sell the software. It might not cost $120 like it used to, but it's certainly not free. If they truly didn't care about selling a Windows license, then Windows 10 would just be free forever, not for the first years for existing customers and also pirates.

I think it will give them some visibility into who is pirating their software too. If someone upgrades non genuine Windows to Windows 10 non genuine, then they will download files etc from a Microsoft server and MS can get metrics from that. I see this as building a bridge between pirates and legit users.

They will probably make it easier for people with pirated versions to buy a legit version as well. I know many people in Asia buy PCs and just know it has Windows, not knowing (or understanding) if legit or not.
Looks like it wasn't pointless to buy the legit licenses after all!
